Team,

Quick pre-read ahead of Monday's planning huddle. Pipeline has three near-term asks that materially impact reserved capacity:

- ACME (pilot -> production): ask = 48 GPUs (A100) starting mid-Sep, initial 8-week pilot then scale to 48 if success. See attached SOW.
- Nimbus (expansion): ask = additional 24 GPUs (T4-equivalent) for burst; procurement prefers monthly commit.
- Orion (PO expected): ask = 16 GPUs, start late Aug.

Attached: weekly_capacity_matrix_Aug03.xlsx (draft numbers) and ACME_SOW_v3.pdf. Please review the matrix and reply with the following by EOD Monday:
  1) Finance: confirm if we can price a 6-week pilot vs a reserved 3-month commit for ACME (Laura).
  2) Infra: confirm pool availability and whether burst slots can cover Nimbus in Sept (Karthik).
  3) Sales: confirm deal start dates and any procurement blockers (Ben).

If anything in the attached numbers looks off, call it out in the thread so I can consolidate before the meeting.

Thanks,
Ben

Thanks Ben — quick finance read:

- ACME: we can structure a 6-week pilot price that converts to a standard reserved contract on day 1 of scale. Pilot pricing will be at ~1.3x hosted list for pilot period; committed pricing available if they sign a 3-month reserve. Need final expected start date and expected steady-state GPU count for the conversion clause.
- Nimbus: finance can approve a short-term burst credit line for up to 30 GPUs for up to 2 weeks, but we prefer turning that into a Reserve if usage exceeds 200k token-hours projected.
- Orion: if PO arrives by Aug 15 we can include them in the September reserved commit batch.

I've attached budget_notes_ACME.docx — includes suggested pilot terms and conversion language. Also flagging that a priced canary (reduced latency SLO) may change unit economics; we should call that out in the SOW.

Laura

Folks,

Quick infra snapshot: attaching pool_availability_snapshot.csv — TL;DR:
- Reserved pool A (us-west-2, A100): 120 GPUs free in Aug, but projected contention during week of Sep 11 if ACME scales to 48 and other pilots hit.
- Burst pool (multi-region, T4 equiv): ~45 slots free in early Sep; can cover Nimbus short-term but will impact burst latency targets.

Recommendations:
1) Pre-allocate 40 GPUs from Reserved pool A (temporary hold) for ACME between Sep 10–Oct 31 to avoid churn; we can release them if not used by Sep 20.
2) For Nimbus, use burst pool for the first two weeks of Sep; if utilization exceeds 70% we need to convert to a reserve or throttle non-critical burst traffic.
3) Consider quantized T4 instances for non-latency-sensitive loads — could save ~30% cost and free A100 slots.

Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.com/fleet/allocations (see section "pre-alloc hold")
